498	## Mermaid Validation Rules
499	
500	LLM-generated mermaid frequently contains syntax errors. After generating the diagram, **check every rule below** before presenting it to the user. Fix violations before outputting.
501	
502	### Syntax Rules
503	
504	1. **First line must be `graph LR`** (horizontal — matches the Flow canvas) — use `graph` not `flowchart` (the `flowchart` keyword is not supported by all renderers).
505	2. **Node IDs must be alphanumeric + underscores only** — no hyphens, dots, or spaces in IDs. Use `fetchData` not `fetch-data` or `fetch.data`
506	3. **Node IDs must not start with or equal a reserved word** — mermaid reserves these as keywords: `end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`. IDs that start with these (e.g., `endWarm`, `defaultPath`, `styleNode`) break the parser. Use alternatives like `warmEnd`, `pathDefault`, `nodeStyle` — or use a prefix like `done_warm`, `finish_warm`.
507	4. **Node labels must be plain text** — no quotes inside shape delimiters. Use `A[Fetch Data]` not `A["Fetch Data"]`.
508	5. **No special characters in labels** — these break mermaid parsing even when quoted:
509	   - `>` and `<` (interpreted as shape operators or HTML) — replace with words like "over" or "under"
510	   - `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` (conflict with shape delimiters)
511	   - `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `"` (unreliable across renderers)
512	   - Use plain alphanumeric text and spaces only
513	6. **Use only universally supported shapes** — `(text)` for rounded rectangle, `[text]` for rectangle, `{text}` for diamond. Do NOT use `([text])` (stadium), `{{text}}` (hexagon), or other extended shapes — they are not supported by all renderers.
514	7. **Edge labels use `|label|` between arrow and target** — `A -->|success| B` not `A -->success B` or `A --success--> B`
515	8. **No empty labels** — `A --> B` is fine, but `A -->|| B` is invalid
516	9. **Subgraph IDs must be unique** and not collide with node IDs
517	10. **Subgraph blocks must be closed** — every `subgraph` needs a matching `end`
518	11. **No semicolons** — mermaid uses newlines, not semicolons, to separate statements
519	12. **No blank lines inside the mermaid block** — blank lines between node definitions and edges can prevent rendering in some mermaid implementations. Keep all lines contiguous.
520	
521	### Structural Rules
522	
523	1. **Every node defined must be connected** — no orphan nodes floating in the diagram
524	2. **Edge directions must match the flow** — trigger at the top, End at the bottom (for TB layouts)
525	3. **Decision nodes must show both branches** — `true` and `false` edges, each labeled
526	4. **Switch nodes must show all case edges** — one per case plus optional default
527	5. **Loop structures**: show the loop body and the loopBack edge returning to the loop node
528	6. **Parallel branches** must visually fork from one node and converge at a Merge node
529	
530	### Validation Procedure
531	
532	After generating the mermaid block:
533	
534	1. First line is `graph LR` — not `flowchart`
535	2. Check each node ID contains only `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`
536	3. Check no node ID starts with or equals a reserved word (`end`, `subgraph`, `graph`, `flowchart`, `direction`, `click`, `style`, `classDef`, `class`, `linkStyle`, `callback`, `default`)
537	4. Check no labels contain `>`, `<`, `:`, `;`, `?`, `&`, `(`, `)`, or quotes — replace with plain words
538	5. Only `(text)`, `[text]`, and `{text}` shapes are used — no `([text])`, `{{text}}`, or other extended shapes
539	6. Check each edge has valid `-->`, `-->|label|` syntax
540	7. Check all subgraphs are closed
541	8. Verify every node in the node table appears in the diagram
542	9. Verify every edge in the edge table appears in the diagram
543	10. Check for blank lines inside the mermaid block — remove any empty lines between statements
544	11. If any rule is violated, fix it before outputting
545	
546	---
547	
548	## Node Selection Heuristics
549	
550	Quick decision guide. For full details, read the linked plugin's `planning.md`.
551	
552	### "I need to call an external service"
553	
554	1. Is there a connector with a curated activity? Run `uip maestro flow registry list --output json` and check for typed nodes matching `uipath.connector.<key>.<operation>`. If the desired operation appears as a node type, it is a curated activity -> [connector](plugins/connector/planning.md)
555	2. Connector exists but the operation is not listed as a curated node type? -> `core.action.http.v2` connector mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
556	3. No connector exists, but has a REST API? -> `core.action.http.v2` manual mode — see [http](plugins/http/planning.md)
557	4. No API at all (desktop app, terminal)? -> [rpa](plugins/rpa/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if unpublished
558	
559	### "I need to branch"
560	
561	- Two paths -> [decision](plugins/decision/planning.md)
562	- Three or more paths -> [switch](plugins/switch/planning.md)
563	- Branch on HTTP response status -> [http](plugins/http/planning.md) built-in branches
564	
565	### "I need to transform data"
566	
567	- Standard map/filter/group-by -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
568	- Custom logic, string manipulation, computation -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md)
569	
570	### "I need to end the flow"
571	
572	- Normal completion -> [end](plugins/end/planning.md) (one per terminal path)
573	- Fatal error, abort everything -> [terminate](plugins/terminate/planning.md)
574	
575	### "I need to wait"
576	
577	- Fixed duration -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
578	- Wait until a specific time -> [delay](plugins/delay/planning.md)
579	- Wait for external work to complete -> [queue](plugins/queue/planning.md) (`create-and-wait`)
580	
581	### "I need human involvement"
582	
583	- Human approval or data entry -> [hitl](plugins/hitl/planning.md) or `core.logic.mock` if the app doesn't exist
584	
585	### "I need an AI agent"
586	
587	- Low-code agent tightly coupled to this flow, bundled inside the flow project -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) (`uipath.agent.autonomous`)
588	- Coded (Python) agent, or any agent that lives as a separate project (in this solution or published to Orchestrator) -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`)
589	
590	### "I need an LLM to process rows of a CSV or summarize a document"
591	
592	- Add LLM-generated columns to every row of a CSV (classify, summarize, extract) -> [batch-transform](plugins/batch-transform/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.batch-transform`)
593	- Synthesize or answer questions over one attached document, with optional citations -> [summarize](plugins/summarize/planning.md) (`uipath.pattern.deep-rag`)
594	- Small ad-hoc reshaping (map/filter/groupBy) without an LLM -> [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
595	- Multi-step reasoning with tool use -> [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md) or [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md)
596	
597	### "I need to extract structured fields from documents"
598	
599	- Source is a PDF, scanned form, photo, or email attachment with **variable layout** across inputs (invoices from many vendors, receipts, contracts, forms) -> [ixp](plugins/ixp/planning.md) (`uipath.ixp.{modelName}.{fullyQualifiedName}`)
600	- Source is already structured (CSV, JSON, database row) -> [script](plugins/script/planning.md) or [transform](plugins/transform/planning.md)
601	- Need free-form summarization, classification, or open-ended reasoning -> [agent](plugins/agent/planning.md) or [inline-agent](plugins/inline-agent/planning.md)
602	- IxP model not yet trained -> use `core.logic.mock` and surface in Open Questions
603	
604	### "The flow needs something outside flow capabilities"
605	
606	1. Add a `core.logic.mock` placeholder
607	2. Note what needs to be created and which skill handles it:
608	   - Desktop/browser automation or coded workflow (C#) -> `uipath-rpa`
609	   - Agent -> `uipath-agents`
610	3. Phase 2 will check whether the resource has been published and replace the mock
611	
612	---
613	
614	## Handoff to Phase 2
615	
616	When the architectural plan is approved, Phase 2 ([Planning Phase 2: Implementation](planning-impl.md)) takes over to:
617	
618	1. Validate all node types via `uip maestro flow registry get` — read each plugin's `impl.md` for registry validation steps
619	2. Resolve connector and resource nodes — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` ([connector](plugins/connector/impl.md), [rpa](plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](plugins/agent/impl.md), etc.)
620	3. Resolve resource nodes (confirm published, get definitions)
621	4. Validate required fields against user-provided values
622	5. Replace `<PLACEHOLDER>` values in the node table with resolved IDs
623	6. Replace `core.logic.mock` nodes with real resource nodes (if now published)
624	7. Finalize the plan with implementation-ready details
625	
626	**Do not proceed to Phase 2 until the user explicitly approves the architectural plan.**

1	# Agent Node — Planning
2	
3	Agent nodes invoke UiPath AI agents from within a flow. Published agents appear in the registry after `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`. **In-solution** (unpublished) agents in sibling projects are discovered via `--local` — no login or publish required. Both **coded** (Python) and **low-code** (agent.json) agents appear here once deployed — the flow treats them identically.
4	
5	> **Related plugin:** [inline-agent](../inline-agent/planning.md) covers low-code agents embedded as a UUID subdirectory **inside** the flow project (`uipath.agent.autonomous`). Coded agents always use this `agent` plugin, not `inline-agent`.
6	
7	> **Choosing between coded and low-code, or wiring them into a flow:** see the `uipath-agents` skill — [coded-vs-lowcode-guide.md](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded-vs-lowcode-guide.md) for the comparison, [coded/flow-integration.md](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/coded/flow-integration.md) for coded-agent Flow patterns.
8	
9	> **If the user names an existing agent, it is a published agent — not inline.** When a prompt says "use the X agent" / "call the Y agent" / "invoke the Z coded agent" / "use the W low-code agent", the user is referring to an agent that already exists in the tenant (or in-solution). ALWAYS run `uip maestro flow registry search "<name>" --output json` BEFORE deciding to scaffold an inline agent. The words "coded" and "low-code" describe the *implementation style* of a published agent — they do NOT mean "inline". Inline (`uipath.agent.autonomous`) is only correct when the user explicitly asks to embed, inline, or create a new agent from scratch inside this flow.
10	
11	## Node Type Pattern
12	
13	`uipath.core.agent.{key}`
14	
15	The `{key}` is the agent's unique identifier (typically a GUID) from Orchestrator.
16	
17	## When to Use
18	
19	Use an Agent node when the flow needs to invoke a published AI agent for reasoning, judgment, or natural language processing.
20	
21	### Agent vs Script/Decision Decision Table
22	
23	| Use an Agent node when... | Use Script/Decision/Switch when... |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| Input is ambiguous or unstructured (free text, emails, support tickets) | Input is structured and well-defined (JSON, form data) |
26	| Task requires reasoning or judgment (triage, classification, summarization) | Task is deterministic (if X then Y, map/filter/transform) |
27	| Branching depends on context that can't be reduced to simple conditions | Branching conditions are explicit and enumerable |
28	| You need natural language generation (draft emails, summaries) | You need data transformation or computation |
29	
30	### Anti-Pattern
31	
32	Don't use an agent node for tasks that can be done with a Decision + Script. Agents are slower, more expensive (LLM tokens), and less predictable. Use them where their flexibility is actually needed.
33	
34	### Hybrid Pattern
35	
36	Use workflow nodes for the deterministic parts (fetch data, transform, route) and agent nodes for the ambiguous parts (classify intent, draft response, extract entities). The flow orchestrates; the agent reasons.
37	
38	### When NOT to Use
39	
40	- **Agent in the same solution but not yet published** — use `--local` discovery (see below)
41	- **Agent does not exist yet** — tell the user to create it in the same solution with `uipath-agents`, then use `--local` discovery
42	- **Task is deterministic** — use [Script](../script/planning.md) or [Decision](../decision/planning.md)
43	- **Need to call an external service API** — use [Connector](../connector/planning.md) or [HTTP](../http/planning.md)
44	- **Agent should be a tool for another agent** — don't use this node; instead add the agent as a tool resource (`uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent`) wired to a parent agent node. See the `uipath-agents` skill for the resource file format
45	
46	## Ports
47	
48	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
49	| --- | --- |
50	| `input` | `output`, `error` |
51	
52	The `error` port is the implicit error port shared with all action nodes — see [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
53	
54	## Output Variables
55	
56	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — the agent's response (contains `content` string)
57	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the agent fails (`code`, `message`, `detail`, `category`, `status`)
58	
59	## Discovery
60	
61	**Published (tenant registry):**
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
65	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent" --output json
66	```
67	
68	Requires `uip login`. Returns published tenant resources only — for in-solution sibling projects, use the `--local` discovery below.
69	
70	**In-solution (local, no login required):**
71	
72	```bash
73	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
74	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
75	```
76	
77	Run from inside the flow project directory. Discovers sibling agent projects in the same `.uipx` solution.
78	
79	## Planning Annotation
80	
81	In the architectural plan:
82	- If the agent exists: note as `resource: <agent-name> (agent)`
83	- If it does not exist: note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` with skill `uipath-agents`
84

1	# Decision Node — Planning
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.decision`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Decision node for binary branching (if/else) based on a boolean condition.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Decision? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Two-path branch based on a boolean condition | Yes |
16	| Three or more paths | No — use [Switch](../switch/planning.md) |
17	| Branch on HTTP response status codes | No — use [HTTP](../http/planning.md) built-in branches |
18	| Branch requires reasoning on ambiguous input | No — use [Agent](../agent/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input` | `true`, `false` |
25	
26	## Key Inputs
27	
28	| Input | Required | Description |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| `expression` | Yes | Boolean JavaScript expression (e.g., `$vars.fetchData.output.statusCode === 200`) |
31	| `trueLabel` | No | Custom label for the true branch |
32	| `falseLabel` | No | Custom label for the false branch |
33	
34	## Wiring Rules
35	
36	- Decision nodes produce exactly **two** outgoing edges: one from `true`, one from `false`
37	- Both branches must lead to a downstream node (no dangling branches)
38	- Each branch typically ends at its own End node or merges back into a shared path

1	# Connector Trigger Nodes — Planning
2	
3	Connector trigger nodes start a flow when an external event fires (e.g., "email received in Outlook", "issue created in Jira"). They use UiPath Integration Service connectors — the same ecosystem as IS activity nodes — but replace the manual/scheduled start node with an event-driven one.
4	
5	> **Two node families, same mechanism:**
6	>
7	> - **Connector trigger** (`uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>`) — **starts** the flow.
8	> - **Wait for events** (`uipath.connector.event.<key>.<event>`) — **pauses a running flow** until the event arrives, then continues. Has an `input` port; NOT the start node. See [Wait for events](impl.md#wait-for-events-uipathconnectoreventkeyevent).
9	
10	## When to Use
11	
12	**Trigger** — flow should start when an external event fires.
13	
14	**Event** (mid-flow) — running flow must wait for an external event before proceeding (sent an approval, waits for the reply). Flow keeps its own start trigger.
15	
16	### Decision Order
17	
18	| Tier | Trigger Type | When to Use |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| 1 | **IS connector trigger** (this node type) | A connector exists and supports the event you need (e.g., "new email", "issue created") |
21	| 2 | **Scheduled trigger** (`core.trigger.scheduled`) | No event trigger exists, but you can poll on a schedule + filter for changes |
22	| 3 | **Manual trigger** (`core.trigger.manual`) | Flow is started on demand by a user or API call |
23	
24	### Prerequisites
25	
26	- `uip login` required — trigger nodes only appear in the registry after authentication
27	- A healthy IS connection must exist for the connector. Before concluding none exists: derive the connector key from a `registry search` node type (never inferred from the service's brand name — the registry key is frequently prefixed or qualified differently), list with `uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json`, and retry once with `--refresh`. An empty result from an unverified key or without `--all-folders` is a false negative, not "no connection." Only when absence is confirmed must the user create one before proceeding.
28	- `uip maestro flow registry pull` must be run to cache trigger node types locally
29	
30	### When NOT to Use
31	
32	- **No connector exists for the service** — use a scheduled trigger with `core.action.http.v2` polling instead
33	- **The event is time-based, not data-driven** — use `core.trigger.scheduled`
34	- **The flow should be started manually** — use `core.trigger.manual`
35	- **You need to react to UiPath Orchestrator queue items** — use a queue trigger (separate mechanism)
36	
37	## Node Type Pattern
38	
39	`uipath.connector.trigger.<connector-key>.<trigger-name>`
40	
41	Examples:
42	- `uipath.connector.trigger.uipath-microsoft-outlook365.email-received`
43	- `uipath.connector.trigger.uipath-atlassian-jira.issue-created`
44	- `uipath.connector.trigger.uipath-salesforce-slack.new-message`
45	
46	## Key Differences from IS Activity Nodes
47	
48	| Aspect | IS Activity | IS Trigger |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| Type pattern | `uipath.connector.<key>.<activity>` | `uipath.connector.trigger.<key>.<trigger>` |
51	| Position in flow | Anywhere (action node) | Start node only (replaces manual trigger) |
52	| `--connection-id` on `registry get` | Optional (enriches metadata) | **Required** (fails without it) |
53	| Metadata returned | `inputDefinition`, `outputResponseDefinition`, `connectorMethodInfo` | `eventParameters`, `filterFields`, `outputResponseDefinition`, `eventMode` |
54	| Configuration | `node configure --detail` (method, endpoint, bodyParameters) | `node configure --detail` (eventMode, eventParameters, filter tree; objectName for generic triggers) |
55	| Bindings | `Connection` resource | `Connection` + `EventTrigger` + `Property` resources (auto-generated) |
56	
57	## Discovery
58	
59	```bash
60	# Search for trigger nodes in the registry
61	uip maestro flow registry search trigger --output json
62	
63	# Or search by service name
64	uip maestro flow registry search outlook trigger --output json
65	```
66	
67	Confirm `tags` includes both `"connector"` and `"trigger"` in the results.
68	
69	If the trigger doesn't appear, re-pull the registry (triggers require authentication):
70	
71	```bash
72	uip login status --output json
73	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
74	```
75	
76	## Ports
77	
78	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
79	|---|---|
80	| — (start node) | `output` |
81	
82	## Output Variables
83	
84	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — the event payload (structure depends on the trigger — see `outputResponseDefinition` from enrichment)
85	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the trigger encounters an issue
86	
87	## Event Mode
88	
89	Triggers operate in one of two modes (returned in `eventMode` from `registry get`):
90	
91	| Mode | Behavior |
92	|---|---|
93	| `webhooks` | The connector registers a webhook — events fire in near-real-time |
94	| `polling` | The runtime polls the service on an interval — slight delay between event and trigger |
95	
96	The agent does not need to configure the mode — it is determined by the connector. Note it in the plan for the user's awareness.
97	
98	> **Debug impact:** Only `polling` triggers can be debugged in Studio Web. `webhooks` triggers cannot be tested via `uip maestro flow debug` — they require deployment to Orchestrator. Flag this in the plan if the trigger uses webhook mode.
99	
100	### Webhook Triggers — Extra Steps
101	
102	When `eventMode` is `"webhooks"`, two additional considerations apply:
103	
104	1. **BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connections.** Some webhook events require BYOA — the customer must register their own OAuth app with the external service. The `byoaConnection` flag on the `triggers objects` response indicates this **per event object**, not per connector. Selection workflow (filter, `--refresh`, stop-and-ask) lives in [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md — For BYOA Connections](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md#for-byoa-connections-webhook-triggers). Flag in the plan if BYOA is required so the user can prepare.
105	
106	2. **Webhook URL registration.** After the trigger is configured (Step 6 in implementation), the webhook URL must be retrieved and registered on the customer's external service. Without registration, the trigger never fires. See [implementation Step 6b](impl.md#step-6b--retrieve-and-display-webhook-url-webhooks-only) and [/uipath:uipath-platform — triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval).
107	
108	## Planning Annotation
109	
110	In the architectural plan, annotate connector trigger nodes as:
111	- `trigger: <service-name>` with the intended event (e.g., "trigger: Outlook — email received")
112	- Record the event mode (`webhooks` or `polling`) if known from discovery
113	- If discovery found no trigger for the event, fall back to `core.trigger.scheduled` + polling or flag the gap in Open Questions
114

1	# Switch Node — Planning
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.switch`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Switch node for multi-way branching (3+ paths) based on ordered case expressions. Cases are evaluated in order; the first `true` case is taken.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Switch? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Three or more paths based on different conditions | Yes |
16	| Simple true/false branch | No — use [Decision](../decision/planning.md) |
17	| Branch on HTTP response status codes | No — use [HTTP](../http/planning.md) built-in branches |
18	| Branch requires reasoning on ambiguous input | No — use [Agent](../agent/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input` | `case-{id}` (dynamic per case), `default` |
25	
26	## Key Inputs
27	
28	| Input | Required | Description |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| `cases` | Yes | Array of `{ id, label, expression }` (min 1 item) |
31	
32	Each case creates a dynamic output port: `case-{item.id}`. An optional `default` port handles unmatched cases.
33	
34	## Wiring Rules
35	
36	- Switch nodes produce one outgoing edge per case + optionally one from `default`
37	- Each case edge uses `sourcePort: "case-{id}"` where `{id}` matches the case's `id` field
38	- Every case branch must lead to a downstream node
39

1	# HITL Node — Planning
2	
3	The flow needs to pause for a human to review, approve, or fill in data. Two node types serve this need — choose based on form complexity and whether an app already exists.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Which HITL Node to Use
8	
9	| Use case | Node type | Form source |
10	| --- | --- | --- |
11	| Inline form designed right now (fields + outcomes defined in the flow) | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` | Schema embedded in node inputs — no app needed |
12	| Existing coded app or Action Center app | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` | Deployed app from Orchestrator |
13	
14	**Prefer `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`** for new flows. It is an OOTB node — no registry discovery, no app publishing, no tenant dependency.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
19	
20	Node type: `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`
21	Available: always — no `uip login` or registry pull required.
22	
23	### When to Select
24	
25	| Situation | Select? |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Manager approval before processing | Yes |
28	| Human reviews extracted data before submission | Yes |
29	| Human resolves exceptions the automation cannot handle | Yes |
30	| Need a quick form with specific fields and outcomes | Yes |
31	| Existing coded/Action Center app should be used | No — use Option 2 |
32	| Fully automated processing, no human involvement | No |
33	
34	### Ports
35	
36	| Input port | Output port |
37	| --- | --- |
38	| `input` | `outcome-completed` |
39	
40	**The output port must be wired.** A node with no edge on `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely.
41	
42	### Output Variables
43	
44	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object containing all output and inOut fields the human filled in
45	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldName}` — individual field value
46	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome's action value (`"Continue"` or `"End"`)
47	
48	### Schema Design
49	
50	The schema defines what the human sees and provides. Three field categories:
51	
52	| Category | Human can… | Use for |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| `inputs` | Read only | Context the human needs to decide |
55	| `outputs` | Write | Data the automation needs back |
56	| `inOuts` | Read + modify | Fields the human can see and optionally correct |
57	
58	Outcomes are the action buttons (e.g., Approve/Reject). First outcome is primary.
59	
60	**In the architectural plan**, describe the schema:
61	```
62	inputs:   [invoiceId (string), amount (number)]
63	outputs:  [decision (string, required)]
64	outcomes: [Approve, Reject]
65	priority: Low
66	```
67	
68	Full JSON format and conversion examples: see [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md).
69	
70	> **Note:** Skills are self-contained — cross-skill references are for documentation context only. The agent uses the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill to implement HITL nodes; this planning guide is for topology selection only.
71	
72	### Wiring Pattern
73	
74	```
75	[Upstream] -> [HITL] ->|outcome-completed| [Continue]
76	```
77	
78	### Common Topology Patterns
79	
80	**Approval gate:**
81	```
82	Trigger -> Fetch Data -> HITL (review) ->|outcome-completed| Decision (approved?) ->
83	  true: Script (process) -> End
84	  false: Script (log rejection) -> End
85	```
86	
87	**Exception escalation:**
88	```
89	Trigger -> Process -> Decision (confidence ok?) ->
90	  true: Continue -> End
91	  false: HITL (exception review) ->|outcome-completed| Script (retry with human input) -> End
92	```
93	
94	### Planning Annotation
95	
96	In the node table:
97	```
98	| hitlReview | Invoice Review | human-task | uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form | inputs: [invoiceId, amount] outputs: [decision] outcomes: [Approve, Reject] | output, status |
99	```
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Option 2 — `uipath.core.human-task.{key}` (App-Based)
104	
105	Node type: `uipath.core.human-task.{key}`
106	Available: tenant-specific resource — requires `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`.
107	
108	### When to Select
109	
110	Use when there is an existing coded app or Action Center app that should be the task form.
111	
112	### Ports
113	
114	| Input port | Output port |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| `input` | `output` |
117	
118	### Output Variables
119	
120	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — form data submitted by the user
121	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if execution fails
122	
123	### Discovery
124	
125	**Published (tenant registry):**
126	
127	```bash
128	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
129	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.human-task" --output json
130	```
131	
132	**In-solution (local, no login required):**
133	
134	```bash
135	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json
136	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --local --output json
137	```
138	
139	Run from inside the flow project directory. Discovers sibling projects in the same `.uipx` solution.
140	
141	### Planning Annotation
142	
143	- If the app exists: note as `resource: <name> (human-task)`
144	- If it does not exist: note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` with skill `uipath-coded-apps`, use `core.logic.mock` placeholder
145

1	# Inline Agent Node — Planning
2	
3	Inline agent nodes embed an autonomous AI agent **inside** the flow project. The agent definition lives as a subdirectory of the flow project and is published together with the flow — no separate agent project, no tenant publishing step. Unlike [published agents](../agent/planning.md), the node type is fixed and the agent is bound to the flow via a local `projectId` rather than a registry-resolved resource key.
4	
5	For agent configuration, prompts, resource files, and solution-resource mechanics, see the `uipath-agents` skill — specifically `lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md`.
6	For coded (Python) agents, use the [`agent`](../agent/planning.md) plugin (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`) — inline agents are low-code only.
7	
8	## Node Type
9	
10	`uipath.agent.autonomous`
11	
12	This is a fixed, OOTB node type (no `{key}` suffix). Inline agents do not appear in `registry search` — the single node type accepts any inline agent via its `inputs.source` field.
13	
14	## When to Use
15	
16	Use an inline agent node when the reasoning/judgment task is tightly scoped to this specific flow and you want the fastest path to a working agent.
17	
18	### Inline vs Published Agent Decision Table
19	
20	| Situation | Inline (`uipath.agent.autonomous`) | Published ([`uipath.core.agent.{key}`](../agent/planning.md)) |
21	| --- | --- | --- |
22	| Agent is specific to this one flow | Yes | No |
23	| Agent will be reused across flows or solutions | No | Yes |
24	| Agent needs independent versioning | No | Yes |
25	| Prototyping — fastest scaffolding | Yes | No |
26	| Agent is already published in the tenant | No — use the published node | Yes |
27	
28	### Anti-Pattern
29	
30	Do not inline an agent you intend to reuse. Inline agents are private to the flow project — if you later need to call the same agent from another flow, you must re-scaffold and re-configure it, diverging over time. Use a published agent for shared logic.
31	
32	**Do NOT scaffold an inline agent to satisfy a prompt that names an existing agent.** If the prompt says "use the X agent" / "call the Y agent" / "invoke the Z coded agent" / "use the W low-code agent", the user is referring to a published agent. Search the tenant registry by name first: `uip maestro flow registry search "<name>" --output json`. Only scaffold inline when the user explicitly asks to **embed / inline / include / create** an agent inside this flow. The words "coded" and "low-code" describe the implementation style of a published agent — they are NOT synonyms for "inline".
33	
34	### When NOT to Use
35	
36	- **Agent already exists as a published tenant resource** — use the [published agent](../agent/planning.md) node instead
37	- **User references the agent by name** (existing agent) — search the tenant registry first; scaffold inline only if the user explicitly asks to embed/inline a new agent
38	- **Task is deterministic** — use [Script](../script/planning.md) or [Decision](../decision/planning.md)
39	
40	## Ports
41	
42	| Port | Position | Direction | Use |
43	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
44	| `input` | left | target | Flow sequence input |
45	| `success` | right | source | Normal flow output |
46	| `error` | right | source | Implicit error port (shared with all action nodes) — see [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) |
47	| `tool` | bottom | source (artifact) | Connect tool resource nodes |
48	| `context` | bottom | source (artifact) | Connect context resource nodes |
49	| `escalation` | top | source (artifact) | Connect escalation resource nodes |
50	
51	## Output Variables
52	
53	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content` — the agent's text response
54	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if the agent fails (`code`, `message`, `detail`, `category`, `status`)
55	
56	## Scaffolding Prerequisite
57	
58	Unlike published agents, inline agents are **not** discovered through the registry — they are created locally inside the flow project before (or during) flow build:
59	
60	```bash
61	uip agent init "<FlowProjectDir>" --inline-in-flow --output json
62	```
63	
64	Record the returned `ProjectId` — the flow node's `inputs.source` must match it exactly.
65	
66	The scaffold sets `settings.model: "gpt-4o-2024-11-20"` (stale) and empty prompts — both are placeholders. During Phase 2 you MUST override the model (`uip agent model list` → newest GA per task) and author a robust system prompt + typed `outputSchema` per the obligations in [impl.md § Configure `agent.json`](impl.md#configure-agentjson). The skeleton, model-discovery command, and production checklist live in the `uipath-agents` skill's `model-selection-guide.md` and `agent-prompting-guide.md` (source of truth).
67	
68	For agent.json configuration (prompts, model, schemas) and resource file authoring (tools, contexts, escalations), see the `uipath-agents` skill (`lowcode/agent-definition.md` and `lowcode/capabilities/`).
69	
70	## Resource Nodes
71	
72	The autonomous agent attaches resource nodes to its three artifact ports: tools (external or built-in) on `tool` (bottom), context on `context` (bottom), escalation on `escalation` (top). Decide which the agent needs at planning time. Full wiring — node JSON, edges, refresh, a single matrix covering all kinds — is in [impl.md § Adding Resource Nodes](impl.md#adding-resource-nodes); `resource.json` bodies are owned by the `uipath-agents` skill (`lowcode/capabilities/`).
73	
74	- **External tool** (`tool` port) — agent calls a deployed automation. Four kinds; discover via the registry below. Needs `uip solution resources refresh`.
75	- **Built-in tool** (`tool` port) — platform-shipped tool, e.g. analyze-attachments. `registry get uipath.agent.resource.tool.builtin.<toolType>`. Self-contained — no bindings, no solution-level files, no `uip solution resources refresh`.
76	- **Context** (`context` port) — RAG retrieval from a Context Grounding index. `registry search "uipath.agent.resource.context"`, then `get` the matching `NodeType`. Needs `uip solution resources refresh`.
77	- **Escalation** (`escalation` port) — human-in-the-loop approval/review mid-run via a deployed Action Center app. `registry get uipath.agent.resource.escalation`. Needs `uip solution resources refresh`.
78	
79	### External tools — registry discovery
80	
81	The four external tool kinds share discovery, `resource.json` shape, and refresh — only the `type` field and the schema flavor differ (see § Subtypes in `process.md`). Pick the prefix per kind:
82	
83	| Kind | Registry-search prefix | `resource.json.type` | What it calls |
84	|------|------------------------|----------------------|---------------|
85	| RPA process | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.process` | `process` | RPA workflow (XAML / coded) |
86	| Agent | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.agent` | `agent` | Low-code or coded agent |
87	| API workflow | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.api` | `api` | Coded API workflow |
88	| Process Orchestration | `uipath.agent.resource.tool.processorchestration` | `processOrchestration` | Agentic / orchestrated process |
89	
90	```bash
91	uip maestro flow registry search "<prefix>" --output json
92	```
93	
94	Filter rows where `NodeType` starts with `<prefix>.` and `DisplayName` matches. The `Description` field disambiguates same-named resources by folder. Fetch the full manifest:
95	
96	```bash
97	uip maestro flow registry get "<NodeType>" --output json
98	```
99	
100	For the tool's `resource.json` format and solution-level resource setup, see the `uipath-agents` skill (`lowcode/capabilities/process/`). Set `location` based on the discovery `Source` field: `"solution"` when `Source: "Local"`, `"external"` when `Source: "Remote"` (same rule as standalone agents — see `critical-rules.md` Rule 12). Set `properties.folderPath` to the **literal folder path from discovery** — parse it from the registry `Description` field (e.g., `(Shared/Sales)` → `"Shared/Sales"`) or from `uip solution resources get`. Do **not** leave `folderPath` empty — an empty `folderPath` prevents `uip solution resources refresh` from resolving the tool at runtime.
101	
102	### Anti-pattern
103	
104	Do not use `uip agent tool add` to attach the tool to an inline-in-flow agent. That command is designed for standalone agent projects. For inline-in-flow agents, hand-author the tool's `resource.json` and let `uip solution resources refresh` materialize the solution-level files.
105	
106	## Planning Annotation
107	
108	In the architectural plan:
109	
110	- `inline-agent: <description>` with a `<projectId-placeholder>` — the UUID is assigned during Phase 2 when `uip agent init --inline-in-flow` runs
111	- `inline-agent-tool: <ToolName> (<kind>, solution|external) → <name> in <folder-path>` — one line per external tool. `<kind>` is one of `process` | `agent` | `api` | `processOrchestration`.
112	- `inline-agent-escalation: <EscalationName> → <AppName> in <folder-path>` — one line per escalation (Action Center HITL).
113	- `inline-agent-context: <ContextName> (index) → <IndexName> in <folder-path>` — one line per context resource.
114	- `inline-agent-builtin-tool: <ToolName> (<toolType>)` — one line per built-in tool; no folder (self-contained).
115	- If an existing published agent already covers the use case, prefer the [published agent](../agent/planning.md) annotation instead
116

# CustomerEmailEscalation — Flow Architecture Plan

## 1. Summary

This flow monitors the support inbox in real time. The moment an email arrives, an inline AI agent classifies it as **urgent**, **high-priority**, or **normal**. Urgent emails are immediately acknowledged and forwarded to the escalation team; high-priority emails are acknowledged and moved to a priority queue folder; normal emails are filed for standard processing. Every path ends cleanly with full error handling on the classification step.

---

## 2. Flow Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    emailTrigger(Instant Email Received)
    classifyAgent[Classify Email Agent]
    extractPriority[Extract Priority]
    routePriority{Route by Priority}
    sendUrgentAck[Send Urgent Acknowledgment]
    forwardEscalation[Forward to Escalation Team]
    markUrgentRead[Mark Email Read]
    doneUrgent(Done Urgent)
    sendHighAck[Send High Priority Acknowledgment]
    moveHighFolder[Move to High Priority Folder]
    doneHigh(Done High Priority)
    moveNormalFolder[Move to Normal Queue Folder]
    doneNormal(Done Normal)
    logClassifyError[Log Classification Error]
    doneError(Done Error)
    emailTrigger -->|output| classifyAgent
    classifyAgent -->|success| extractPriority
    classifyAgent -->|error| logClassifyError
    extractPriority -->|success| routePriority
    extractPriority -->|error| logClassifyError
    routePriority -->|case-urgent| sendUrgentAck
    routePriority -->|case-high| sendHighAck
    routePriority -->|default| moveNormalFolder
    sendUrgentAck -->|output| forwardEscalation
    forwardEscalation -->|output| markUrgentRead
    markUrgentRead -->|output| doneUrgent
    sendHighAck -->|output| moveHighFolder
    moveHighFolder -->|output| doneHigh
    moveNormalFolder -->|output| doneNormal
    logClassifyError -->|success| doneError
```

---

## 3. Node Table

| # | Node ID | Name | Category | Node Type | Inputs | Outputs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `emailTrigger` | Instant Email Received | trigger | `uipath.connector.trigger.uipath-mock-outlook.instant-email-received` | connection (mock-outlook) | `output` — email payload (subject, body, sender, messageId) | webhook mode — fires instantly; requires mock-outlook connection |
| 2 | `classifyAgent` | Classify Email Agent | agent | `uipath.agent.autonomous` | email subject + body from trigger output | `output.content` — JSON string `{priority, summary, customerName}`, `error` | inline agent; scaffold with `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`; Phase 2: author system prompt |
| 3 | `extractPriority` | Extract Priority | action | `core.action.script` | script parses `$vars.classifyAgent.output.content` | `output.priority` (urgent/high/normal), `output.summary`, `output.customerName` | JS: `return JSON.parse($vars.classifyAgent.output.content)` |
| 4 | `routePriority` | Route by Priority | control | `core.logic.switch` | cases on `$vars.extractPriority.output.priority` | `case-urgent`, `case-high`, `default` | 2 explicit cases + default for normal |
| 5 | `sendUrgentAck` | Send Urgent Acknowledgment | action | `uipath.connector.uipath-mock-outlook.reply-to-email` | messageId, body: "We've received your urgent request and are escalating immediately" | `output` | Phase 2: bind connection, resolve message ID field |
| 6 | `forwardEscalation` | Forward to Escalation Team | action | `uipath.connector.uipath-mock-outlook.forward-email` | messageId, toRecipients: `<ESCALATION_TEAM_EMAIL>`, comment | `output` | Phase 2: escalation team email address needed |
| 7 | `markUrgentRead` | Mark Email Read | action | `uipath.connector.uipath-mock-outlook.mark-email-read-or-unread` | messageId, isRead: true | `output` | Prevents duplicate processing |
| 8 | `doneUrgent` | Done Urgent | control | `core.control.end` | — | — | Terminal node for urgent path |
| 9 | `sendHighAck` | Send High Priority Acknowledgment | action | `uipath.connector.uipath-mock-outlook.reply-to-email` | messageId, body: "Your request has been prioritized. Expect a response within 4 hours." | `output` | Phase 2: bind connection |
| 10 | `moveHighFolder` | Move to High Priority Folder | action | `uipath.connector.uipath-mock-outlook.move-email` | messageId, destinationFolderId: `<HIGH_PRIORITY_FOLDER_ID>` | `output` | Phase 2: resolve folder ID via `uip is resources run` |

Here's the architectural plan for your automated customer support email flow. Before I build anything, I want you to review and approve the design:

---

## 📋 CustomerEmailEscalation — Flow Architecture Plan

### What it does

The moment a support email hits your inbox, a UiPath AI agent reads and classifies it as **urgent**, **high-priority**, or **normal**. Based on that classification:

- **Urgent** → Customer gets an immediate reply, the email is forwarded to your escalation team, and it's marked read to prevent double-handling.
- **High Priority** → Customer gets a "within 4 hours" reply, email is moved to a dedicated high-priority folder.
- **Normal** → Email is routed to your standard support queue folder.

```mermaid
graph LR
    emailTrigger(Instant Email Received)
    classifyAgent[Classify Email Agent]
    extractPriority[Extract Priority]
    routePriority{Route by Priority}
    sendUrgentAck[Send Urgent Acknowledgment]
    forwardEscalation[Forward to Escalation Team]
    markUrgentRead[Mark Email Read]
    doneUrgent(Done Urgent)
    sendHighAck[Send High Priority Acknowledgment]
    moveHighFolder[Move to High Priority Folder]
    doneHigh(Done High Priority)
    moveNormalFolder[Move to Normal Queue Folder]
    doneNormal(Done Normal)
    logClassifyError[Log Classification Error]
    doneError(Done Error)
    emailTrigger -->|output| classifyAgent
    classifyAgent -->|success| extractPriority
    classifyAgent -->|error| logClassifyError
    extractPriority -->|success| routePriority
    extractPriority -->|error| logClassifyError
    routePriority -->|case-urgent| sendUrgentAck
    routePriority -->|case-high| sendHighAck
    routePriority -->|default| moveNormalFolder
    sendUrgentAck -->|output| forwardEscalation
    forwardEscalation -->|output| markUrgentRead
    markUrgentRead -->|output| doneUrgent
    sendHighAck -->|output| moveHighFolder
    moveHighFolder -->|output| doneHigh
    moveNormalFolder -->|output| doneNormal
    logClassifyError -->|success| doneError
```

### Key design decisions
| Component | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Webhook (`instant-email-received`) | Fires the moment an email arrives — no polling delay |
| **Classification** | Inline AI agent | Email content is unstructured text — needs AI reasoning, not rules |
| **Routing** | Switch node (3-way) | Three distinct paths: urgent / high / normal |
| **Error handling** | Wired `error` port on agent + script | Flow survives classification failures without crashing |

### What's needed to build this

**[REQUIRED]** Your tenant currently has no Outlook connection configured. You'll need to create one in Integration Service. *(This plan uses the `uipath-mock-outlook` connector available on your tenant — it simulates real Outlook 365 behavior.)*

2. **Which Outlook folder for high-priority emails?** (e.g. "High Priority Queue" — I'll resolve the folder ID)
3. **Which Outlook folder for normal emails?** (e.g. "Support Queue")

And one design question:

4. **Should normal emails also get an auto-reply acknowledgment**, or just be silently moved to the folder?

---

**Does this plan look right to you?** Choose how to proceed:

1. **Approve plan and I'll start building now** *(with placeholder values for the open questions — you can update them later)*
2. **I want to tweak the design first** *(tell me what to change)*

commands.result_summary:
1	# Inline Agent Node — Implementation
2	
3	This plugin covers **flow-specific** operations for inline agent nodes: adding the node, wiring edges, JSON structure, and flow validation. For agent-side concerns (agent.json configuration, resource.json authoring, solution resources, prompts), see the `uipath-agents` skill — specifically `lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md`.
4	
5	Node type: `uipath.agent.autonomous`. The agent is bound to a local subdirectory via `inputs.source = <projectId>`. The node's BPMN type and `serviceType` (`Orchestrator.StartInlineAgentJob`) come from the definition in `definitions[]`.
6	
7	For coded (Python) agents, use the [`agent`](../agent/impl.md) plugin (`uipath.core.agent.{key}`) — inline agents are low-code only.
8	
9	## Prerequisite — Scaffold the Inline Agent
10	
11	```bash
12	uip agent init "<FlowProjectDir>" --inline-in-flow --output json
13	```
14	
15	This creates `<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId-uuid>/` with:
16	
17	- `agent.json` — agent definition (model, prompts, schemas)
18	- `flow-layout.json` — empty `{}`
19	- `evals/eval-sets/` — empty
20	- `features/` — empty
21	- `resources/` — empty (add tool resource files here later)
22	
23	**Record the returned `ProjectId`** — the flow node's `inputs.source` must match it exactly. The same UUID is also the subdirectory name and the `projectId` field inside `agent.json`.
24	
25	For agent.json configuration and resource file setup, see the `uipath-agents` skill (`lowcode/agent-definition.md`, `lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md`).
26	
27	## Configure `agent.json`
28	
29	`uip agent init --inline-in-flow` scaffolds `agent.json` with `settings.model: "gpt-4o-2024-11-20"` (stale) and empty `messages[].content` by design. **Both are placeholders — override them.** A scaffolded inline agent left on the default model with toy prompts is the single biggest quality gap a customer ships. Edit `<FlowProjectDir>/<projectId>/agent.json`:
30	
31	1. **Override the model** — never ship `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`. Discover the tenant's models with `uip agent model list` and pick the newest GA model for the task; set `settings.maxTokens` ≤ its cap. Discovery command, GA filter, and task→model mapping: the `uipath-agents` skill's [`model-selection-guide.md`](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/lowcode/model-selection-guide.md).
32	2. Set `settings.temperature` (0 for extraction/classification/judgment) and `settings.maxIterations` (default 25; lower for single-shot).
33	3. **Write a real system prompt** in `messages[0].content` — bounded role, per-tool call/stop criteria, output contract, grounding. Skeleton + worked example: [`agent-prompting-guide.md`](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/lowcode/prompting/agent-prompting-guide.md).
34	4. Write the user prompt in `messages[1].content`.
35	5. **Declare a typed `outputSchema`** — not a bare `content` string — so downstream nodes can consume the result.
36	
37	After editing `content`, rebuild the matching `messages[].contentTokens` (`type: "simpleText"` / `type: "variable"`). Token mechanics are flow-specific — see § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts below; for prompt-quality structure see `agent-prompting-guide.md`.
38	
39	> **Source of truth.** The prompt skeleton, the production-field checklist (`outputSchema` / `temperature` / `maxIterations` / `guardrails`), the model-discovery command, and the worked example all live in the `uipath-agents` guides linked above — this skill points at them rather than copying, to avoid cross-skill drift. The obligations in steps 1–5 are the build-time minimum; the *how* is one click away.

41	## Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts
42	
43	Passing flow data into an inline agent requires **three hand-authored, aligned** pieces. **The CLI does not derive the input wiring** — `uip agent refresh` does **not** scan prompts, derive `inputSchema`, or populate `agentInputVariables`; you author all three, and packaging ships them as-authored. (Refresh *does* regenerate `messages[].contentTokens` from `content` — that's the one derived part; see the invariant below.) The converter builds the runtime `JobArguments` from the **flow node's `inputs.agentInputVariables[]`** (not from `$vars` tokens in `agent.json`). Flatten rule: `$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>` → `<trigger>__output__<var>`.
44	
45	The three pieces — **Delivery** (node `agentInputVariables[]`), **Contract** (`agent.json` `inputSchema`), and **Resolution** (`{{input.<key>}}` in `messages[].content`) — and their examples are in the table below. `flow validate` catches a Resolution↔Contract mismatch (a `{{input.K}}` that's malformed or names a key not in `inputSchema`), but a missing/wrong **Delivery** binding passes validate and only shows up as empty input at `flow debug`. Agent-side `inputSchema`/`contentTokens` mechanics: the `uipath-agents` skill's [inline-in-flow § Wiring Flow Inputs Into an Inline Agent](../../../../../../uipath-agents/references/lowcode/capabilities/inline-in-flow/inline-in-flow.md#wiring-flow-inputs-into-an-inline-agent-required).
46	
47	> **Prerequisite — the bound value must actually exist as a variable.** A node binding `=$vars.X` resolves at runtime only if `$vars.X` is a declared variable. `flow validate` does **not** check that the path exists — a binding referencing an undeclared trigger field passes validate, then **faults at debug** with `JobArguments` empty. When the upstream node is a **trigger** (e.g. `core.trigger.manual`, id `start`), each field you bind must be declared in `variables.globals[]` as a trigger-associated input — `direction: "in"`, `triggerNodeId: "<triggerId>"` — and is then read as `$vars.<triggerId>.output.<id>`:
48	>
49	> ```json
50	> { "id": "invoiceNumber", "direction": "in", "type": "string", "triggerNodeId": "start" }
51	> ```
52	>
53	> Bind it on the agent node (`agentInputVariables[]`, `=$vars.start.output.invoiceNumber`) and reference it in the prompt as `{{input.start__output__invoiceNumber}}`. Likewise, flow outputs the agent feeds (e.g. `determination`, `rationale`) must be declared as `direction: "out"` globals and mapped on every reachable End node. Full schema and the `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` access rule: [../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) (§ Input associated with a trigger); declaring/mapping mechanics: [../../editing-operations-json.md § Add a workflow variable](../../editing-operations-json.md#add-a-workflow-variable).
54	
55	| Where | What | Example |
56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	| Flow node `inputs.agentInputVariables[]` | One entry per input — the delivery binding the converter turns into `JobArguments`. | `{ "id": "start__output__invoiceNumber", "type": "string", "binding": "=$vars.start.output.invoiceNumber", "description": "Bound from $vars.start.output.invoiceNumber" }` |
58	| `agent.json` `inputSchema.properties` | One `<trigger>__output__<var>` key per input — **mandatory**, binds `JobArguments` → the agent's `input`. | `"start__output__invoiceNumber": { "type": "string", "description": "Bound from $vars.start.output.invoiceNumber" }` |
59	| `agent.json` `messages[].content` | `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` (the `input.` form — never `$vars`). | `"Invoice: {{input.start__output__invoiceNumber}}"` |
60	| `agent.json` `messages[].contentTokens[]` | One `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": "input.<trigger>__output__<var>" }` per `{{ ... }}` token in `content` (brace-free `rawString`). | `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": "input.start__output__invoiceNumber" }` |
61	
62	Each binding's source `$vars.<node>.output.<field>` must reference a real node `id` in the `.flow` file, with an edge path reaching the inline-agent node. See [../../../../shared/node-output-wiring.md](../../../../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the full expression contract.
63	
64	### The `content` ↔ `contentTokens` mirror invariant
65	
66	`content` is the source of truth. **`uip agent refresh` regenerates `messages[].contentTokens` from `content`** (correct `simpleText`/`variable` types, brace-free `rawString`). So: author the prompt in `content`, run `refresh`, and **don't hand-author or hand-fix `contentTokens`**. `uip agent validate` is read-only — if it flags a token mismatch (`Expected type "simpleText"…`, `Expected "input.X" but got "{{input.X}}"`, or `contentTokens has N entries but content requires M`), **re-run `refresh`** to regenerate; don't edit `rawString`.
67	
68	What `refresh` produces, for `content` = `"Invoice Number: {{input.start__output__invoiceNumber}}\n"`:
69	
70	```json
71	"contentTokens": [
72	  { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "Invoice Number: " },
73	  { "type": "variable",   "rawString": "input.start__output__invoiceNumber" },
74	  { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "\n" }
75	]
76	```
77	
78	### Worked example — end to end (repeat the triple per input)
79	
80	Flow node (excerpt) — `binding` per input, typed `agentOutputVariables`:
81	
82	```json
83	"agentInputVariables": [
84	  { "id": "emailReceived1__output__subject", "type": "string", "binding": "=$vars.emailReceived1.output.subject" },
85	  { "id": "emailReceived1__output__body",    "type": "string", "binding": "=$vars.emailReceived1.output.body" }
86	],
87	"agentOutputVariables": [{ "id": "category", "type": "string" }]
88	```
89	
90	Matching `agent.json` — `inputSchema` keys mirror the bindings; the prompt uses the `input.` form, and `contentTokens` decompose `content` left-to-right (literals → `simpleText` verbatim incl. `\n`; each `{{ … }}` → brace-free `variable`):
91	
92	```json
93	"inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": {
94	  "emailReceived1__output__subject": { "type": "string" },
95	  "emailReceived1__output__body":    { "type": "string" }
96	} },
97	"outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "category": { "type": "string" } }, "required": ["category"] },
98	"messages": [
99	  { "role": "system", "content": "Triage the email.", "contentTokens": [{ "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "Triage the email." }] },
100	  { "role": "user",
101	    "content": "Subject: {{input.emailReceived1__output__subject}}\n\n{{input.emailReceived1__output__body}}",
102	    "contentTokens": [
103	      { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "Subject: " },
104	      { "type": "variable",   "rawString": "input.emailReceived1__output__subject" },
105	      { "type": "simpleText", "rawString": "\n\n" },
106	      { "type": "variable",   "rawString": "input.emailReceived1__output__body" }
107	    ] }
108	]
109	```
110	
111	Keep the flow-node `systemPrompt` / `userPrompt` as short generic placeholders — the canonical prompt lives in `agent.json messages[]`, and that system prompt should be a real structured one (see `agent-prompting-guide.md`), not a bare blob.
112	
113	### When the source field name is unknown at authoring time
114	
115	Connector-trigger output fields (e.g. email `subject`/`from`/`body`) aren't in the registry — only knowable after a real run. Author best-guess `{{input.<node>__output__<field>}}` paths with the matching `binding`/`inputSchema` key, **ask the user to confirm before upload** (don't invent field names silently), and correct the tokens + `contentTokens` mirrors after the first run.
116	
117	### Anti-patterns
118	
119	- **In `agent.json` prompts, use the `{{input.<trigger>__output__<var>}}` form** (the flattened key, `input.` prefix). Never use raw `{{ $vars.X }}` (the runtime can't resolve it — agent gets the literal token) or `{{plainName}}` (no prefix).
120	- **The `variable` `rawString` is exactly what sits between the braces** — `input.<trigger>__output__<var>`, brace-free, no added spaces.
121	- **Keep the flow-node `inputs.systemPrompt` / `inputs.userPrompt` as short generic placeholders** — the canonical prompt lives in `agent.json messages[]`, and delivery comes from `agentInputVariables[]`, not from tokens in the node prompts.
122	- **Each `agentInputVariables[]` entry uses `binding` (not `value`).** The converter builds `JobArguments` from `binding`; a `value: "=js:$vars…"` entry (Studio Web's internal canvas form) is **ignored** — the agent gets empty input and faults at debug (`AGENT_RUNTIME.TERMINATION_LLM_RAISED_ERROR`, "Template placeholders detected instead of actual values"). Write `{ "id": "<key>", "binding": "=$vars.<trigger>.output.<var>" }`. `binding` is what both the CLI converter and Studio Web's loader read.
123

141	## Adding / Editing
142	
143	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Inline-agent scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but the flow graph is not a Flow CLI carve-out: add the `uipath.agent.autonomous` node, its `inputs.source`, outputs, variables, layout, and edges directly in the `.flow` JSON with `Edit` / `Write`.
144	
145	### Add the node with Edit / Write
146	
147	Use `Edit` to add a node instance to `nodes[]`. The instance carries only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). BPMN type, serviceType, version, and context templates come from the definition in `definitions[]`. Do not write a node instance `model` block for `uipath.agent.autonomous`: flow-core's `createNodeFromManifest` hoists manifest-declared `source` identity into `inputs.source` and returns a node with no `model`.

150	{
151	  "id": "autonomousAgent1",
152	  "type": "uipath.agent.autonomous",
153	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
154	  "display": { "label": "Autonomous Agent" },
155	  "inputs": {
156	    "systemPrompt": "You are an agentic assistant.",
157	    "userPrompt": "What is the current date?",
158	    "source": "<projectId-uuid>",
159	    "agentInputVariables": [],
160	    "agentOutputVariables": [
161	      { "id": "content", "type": "string" }
162	    ]
163	  },
164	  "outputs": {
165	    "output": {
166	      "type": "object",
167	      "description": "Agent response",
168	      "source": "=result.response",
169	      "var": "output"
170	    },
171	    "error": {
172	      "type": "object",
173	      "description": "Error information if the node fails",
174	      "source": "=Error",
175	      "var": "error"
176	    }
177	  }
178	}
179	```

183	- A `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get uipath.agent.autonomous --output json` (`Data.Node` or the top-level node object, depending on CLI/plugin version). Set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
184	- `variables.nodes[]` entries for `autonomousAgent1.output` and `autonomousAgent1.error` with `binding.nodeId = "autonomousAgent1"` and matching `binding.outputId` values.

188	
189	Use `Edit` to add edge objects to `edges[]`:
190

192	{
193	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
194	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
195	  "sourcePort": "output",
196	  "targetNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",
197	  "targetPort": "input"
198	}

203	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
204	  "sourceNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",

207	  "targetPort": "input"
208	}

214	{
215	  "id": "<EDGE_ID>",
216	  "sourceNodeId": "autonomousAgent1",
217	  "sourcePort": "tool",
218	  "targetNodeId": "<toolNodeId>",
219	  "targetPort": "input"
220	}
